title: Agent Sprite Forge shared contract types
description: Frozen contracts, version 1. Building blocks referenced by the sprite, video, map, codeart and media schemas. Canonical copy in shared/schemas; tools/vendor_sync.py copies it byte for byte into skills/*/references/schemas. Objects stay open (additionalProperties true): producers may add optional fields. Pixel boxes are half-open [x0, y0, x1, y1); paths are manifest-relative POSIX.

relPath.description: Manifest-relative POSIX path: forward slashes only, no leading slash, no drive letter and no URL scheme. '..' segments are allowed. Inputs on another drive record their file name plus sha256.

fileRef.description: A file the document depends on, bound to its content by sha256.

toolInfo.description: A tool or renderer and its exact version.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time with an explicit offset, for example 2026-10-05T04:16:00Z.

qaStatus.description: Overall verdict of a QA document. needs-visual-review means the numbers passed but a human or agent must still look.

qaCheck.description: One measured check. value and threshold are whatever the check measures (number, list, boolean or null). An ungated measurement is a skipped check with its value and a null threshold. Checks stay open: tools add keys such as subject (the file a per-file check is about; pixel_reduce), files (the files it names; palette_tool build), failing (the files or frames over the gate), profile (the lint profile), detail (extra figures such as loop_seam's seam and adjacent_median) and note (autotile_build).

qaEnvelope.description: Every QA JSON states its method, what it does not prove, and the sha256 of every input and output it judged. A pass envelope cannot contain a failed check. createdAt is optional so QA files can stay byte-deterministic. Envelopes stay open: a tool adds its own top-level figures beside the envelope keys (for example palette_tool's palette, fit, totals, locked_inputs and luts, pixel_qa's frames and palette, autotile_build's metrics, parallax_build's seams, sweep and layers).

artSource.description: Where the art came from. Record a separate boolean placeholder for stand-in art.

provenance.description: How an output was produced: the tool, its version, the parameters and the hashed inputs.

box.description: Half-open pixel box [x0, y0, x1, y1) in the PIL convention: x1 and y1 are exclusive.

rectXYWH.description: Rectangle [x, y, width, height] with its top-left corner at (x, y).

padding4.description: Padding [left, top, right, bottom] in whole pixels.

polygon.description: A closed polygon as at least three [x, y] vertices; the last vertex joins the first.

hexColor.description: #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA where AA 00 marks an erasing palette entry.

rgb.description: An [r, g, b] colour with 8-bit channels.

color.description: A colour as a hex string or an [r, g, b] triple.

keyColor.description: A chroma-key colour: a declared key name or an explicit colour.

eventName.description: Gameplay event names shared by clips, selections and runtimes; anything else uses the custom: prefix.

fpsValue.description: Frame rate as a positive number or an exact rational string such as 24000/1001.

durationsMs.description: Per-frame durations in whole milliseconds (forge_core.frame_durations sums exactly to the clip length).

loopPolicy.description: cycle repeats from the first frame, pingpong mirrors without duplicating end frames, oneshot plays once and holds.

sampling.description: Runtime texture sampling: nearest for pixel art, linear for painted art.

shadow.description: Ground shadow ellipse in source pixels, centred on the root.

seamReport.description: forge_core.seam_report of a loop, for QA envelopes of loop tools: seam is the premultiplied RGBA mean absolute difference (0-255) of the wrap (last -> first) and adjacent_* describe the steps between neighbours. seam_over_median and seam_over_p95 near 1 mean a seamless loop, well above 1 a pop at the wrap, near 0 a held duplicate frame; denominators are floored at 1e-6, so a static clip with a pop gives a very large ratio. Measure the decoded runtime file, inside the motion mask for scene loops; pass/fail thresholds belong to the adopting tool.

edgeSeam.description: forge_core.edge_seam_report of one join or wrap: the one seam metric of every tool that judges edges (per D9: platform-strip joins, terrain wraps and Wang joins, parallax repeat seams). The common seamReport of the premultiplied RGBA steps (0-255) across the join (seam) and of the interior steps near it (adjacent_*), plus seam_ratio, near_median and a verdict. seam_ratio is the larger of seam / adjacent_max and the worst few-row window of the join over the worst window of the interior steps near it: about 1 or less looks like the art, well above 1 is a seam; method states the windows. Verdicts (snake_case): continuous (the join steps like the art around it), seam (a visible jump), duplicate_edge (a join much flatter than its neighbourhood: a repeated edge, a one-pixel stutter that edge equality would pass), flat (no measurable steps near the join, so there is nothing to compare) and too_small (fewer than two columns or rows to compare; the numbers may then be absent). A statistic, never a seamlessness proof; pass/fail gates belong to the adopting tool.

cropBoxes.description: forge-crop-boxes/v1 (DOC-18): the one form of measured crop boxes in sheet pixels for every tool. Each item is a half-open integer box [x0, y0, x1, y1) inside the sheet with an optional id. extract_prop_pack writes it as auto-boxes.json (with source, display_name and anchor_px in box pixels) and reads it with --boxes-file, where every item needs an id (the prop label) and may also carry footprint, solid, contact, occlusion_class and occupant_policy as in a prop pack item; assemble_frames --crop-boxes reads it with the id optional. Readers also accept the legacy forms: a bare list of boxes (assemble_frames) and {props: [{label, source_box}]} (extract_prop_pack).

anchor_px.description: The prop's anchor in box pixels.
